Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University (XJTLU)

Xi’an Jiaotong-Liverpool University (XJTLU) is a unique Higher Education institution located in Suzhou, Jiangsu Province, China.

It is the largest international collaborative university in China, established in 2006 by its parent institutions, the University of Liverpool (UK) and Xi’an Jiaotong University (China).


XJTLU is an independent University with degree awarding powers under the Chinese Ministry of Education.

XJTLU enrolls Chinese students through the ‘’Gaokao’’ national examination system (tier 1 students) and international students through independent admissions.

XJTLU is situated on a purpose built campus in the Dushu Lake Higher Education Town, at the heart of one of Asia’s research and innovation hubs.

Markers of XJTLU’s quality can be seen through the high rankings of both of parent Universities; both nationally and internationally well regarded.
administrative:
1. Application dossier

You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application.

Your host university may ask for the following documents:

  • Copy of passport
  • An identity photo
  • Letter of motivation in English / a study plan (explain your choice of classes)
  • Letter of recommendation (written in English)
  • Your transcripts in English (they will be provided directly to the partner university by the IAFF team)
  • Tepitech score certificate downloadable from the intra


To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract.
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier.

This information is subject to change by the partner university.

They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Student Visa

XJTLU posts out original copies of Admission Notice and JW202 Form to students. (within 4 weeks after students receive digital copy of Admission Notice). Students apply for student visa (X visa) to China embassy with original copy of Admissions Notice and JW202 Form.

You must take the necessary steps in obtaining a study visa type X1 upon receipt of the letter of admission and the form JW202 (sent to you by email). Please check this site for more information. Price: between 110 and 130€ (2025). You can also entrust the file to an agency by clicking here.


The X1 visa is an entry visa valid for 3 months from the date of entry into China. After your arrival, you must obtain a Chinese residence permit within 30 days of entering China.


The host university will assist you with visa conversion procedures, medical examinations, and obtaining the resident permit.

Related costs are the responsibility of the students (see estimated budget at the bottom of the page).

Please note:

  • For the latest information regarding visa application, you should contact your nearest Embassy/Consulate of China.
  • After you arrive in the Chinese mainland, the X visa for single entry cannot allow you to exit and re-enter the Chinese mainland. You must stay in the Chinese mainland until the Residence Permit is granted.


3. Insurance and Health

You will be asked to undergo medical examinations after arriving in Xi'An.

The costs of these exams will be borne by the student.


Public hospitals and insurance:

The medical insurance provided by XJTLU covers treatment in public hospitals. Public hospitals in Suzhou are generally clean and reliable.

Due to language barrier and different registration procedures in hospitals, students are advised to take a Chinese speaker with them when they go.

If required, International Student Support Team at XJTLU can arrange a staff member or a student volunteer to assist international students.

Students need to keep all the receipts/invoices and paperwork related to the hospital visit in order to claim back the expenses, either against their own insurance or the one provided by XJTLU.


Private clinics

Private clinics are more foreigner-friendly. Doctors are generally either international or have a high standard of English.

Treatment is entirely western medicine based.

Private clinics are significantly more expensive than public hospitals (examples: Jiahui Health, Sing Health Medical and NewLife Clinic). The insurance provided by XJTLU does not cover private clinics.


Dentist services

There is a dental clinic close to XJTLU campus. All major hospitals provide dentist services.

The insurance provided by XJTLU does not cover dental treatments.


Pharmacy

There are 2 pharmacies near XJTLU campus, both within 15 minutes’ walk from campus.

The pharmacies provide a range of Western and Chinese medicines. Staff don’t speak English, so students should have the name of the medicine written in Chinese, or take a Chinese friend when they go.


Students should always check the chemical name on the information sheet inside the box.

Certain medicines may only be available in major hospitals or private clinics.


In order to be fully covered for medical care, we recommend that you take out international insurance as well. It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.

For more information, please check the country's health forms here: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/chine

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


4.Prepare your arrival

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on China, click here.
accomodation:
On-campus accommodation (click here)

Dormitories for students in both XJTLU SIP Campus and XJTLU Entrepreneur College (Taicang) are provided and managed by independent accommodation providers. Currently, the accommodation facilities are managed privately by the Suzhou Industrial Park Education Development and Investment Limited Company. They are not owned or managed directly by the university, but we communicate with them on your behalf. If you want to live in the Parfait International Apartments or Wenhua Apartments, we will assist in booking your room once you have paid your deposit to secure your place at XJTLU.


The accommodation provider offers two types of contracts. The first is for your first semester and the second is for the full academic year. If you only sign for the first semester, we cannot guarantee you will be able to renew your contract for the second. If you leave the accommodation before the contract ends, you may lose all or a part of your deposit which you will when you check in at the reception.

You must pay for utilities separately, namely electricity and water. Bills is run on a pay-as you-go system. Students should top up at the reception desk.


You also need to arrange for an internet connection with your own contract, but this is easily and quickly done from one of any number of local suppliers.


Please note depending on the length of the tenancy contract, summer school students pay different rates and deposits. Please refer to the arrangements for summer school arrivals for detailed information.


All dormitory rooms, which were built in different years, are equipped with bathrooms, furniture, air-conditioning, water heaters, public laundry rooms and so on to cater to students’ day to day requirements. Outside the dormitory area, public transportation, restaurants/canteens, stores, hospitals, banks, gymnasiums, and libraries are within students’ easy reach. You need to provide your own bedding (pillow, sheets, quilt, blankets – the mattresses are 1.1m x 2m in size). A limited number of bedding packs are available for sale at reception (first come, first served) for 500RMB ($70USD). Alternatively, you can buy all of your bedding needs cheaply at the Wencui Neighborhood Centre supermarkets, which are just a few minutes walk from reception. You can also choose to bring bedding with you.

Parfait International Apartments: It costs 57RMB ($8USD) per day. Rent needs to be paid every 3 months.

Parfait Hotel & Apartments: between 11 and 13USD per day. Rent needs to be paid every 3 months.

Wenhua Apartments: between 11 and 17USD per day. Rent needs to be paid every 3 months.

Please note that upon check-in, deposits and initial utility payments can only be made using cash, WeChat or Alipay. For fees, please refer to the link above.


Off-campus accommodation

You can also arrange to rent a private apartment near the university, either alone or with friends. The easiest way to do this is to employ a local accommodation agent, and there are many of these. The standard agent fee for finding you an apartment is 2 weeks’ rent per year, but this usually includes managing your rental agreement, helping with paying bills and setting up services such as television and internet, and helping with any problems that might arise.


Notes:

  • always keep copies of all payments and the contract;
  • always sign a contract. Without a contract you have no legal rights;
  • when you live off-campus, never forget to register at your local police station to obtain a Registration Form of Temporary Residence within 24 hours after your arrival in China or signing of the rental contract.

cost:
Financial Overview (4th year Epitech)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the tuition fees for the university.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other expenses

  • Roundtrip flight: from 800€
  • Insurance: 300-600€ depending on the coverage
  • Visa: between 110-130€
  • Non-refundable service charge (ID card, airport pick-up, insurance and logistical costs of induction processes):
  • 300 RMB per semester / 600 RMB per academic year (40-70€)

Additionally, you should also allocate funds for the following costs:

  • Rent deposit and initial utilities (varies from place to place, usually one month’s worth of rent).
  • 2,000 RMB/year or 1,000 RMB/semester to cover service charges (for example, textbooks, ID card, printing, etc.).
  • Travel costs (for example, bus, taxi, train, flight).


Monthly Living Expenses (estimations by XJTLU here)

The local currency is the Yuan (RMB or CNY). 1 € = 8.26 RMB (rate as of October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.

Generally, students should plan for USD 600–1200 monthly for living expenses, depending on your consumption capacity.

  • Housing + utilities: about 250€ + 40€
  • Food: 240€
  • Transport: 35€
  • Phone, internet: 15€
  • If you’re with Free Mobile, their €20/month plan includes some roaming data in China, which can be very helpful for the first few days. Otherwise, you can easily buy a local eSIM or a China Unicom SIM card at the airport for short-term use.
  • Leisure: 100-150€

These prices are indicative and may vary.


Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

  • Get a good VPN. Internet restrictions in China can be tricky, so a reliable VPN is essential. Students have mentioned the following three, which work consistently well: MullvadVPN, Let’sVPN, and ChamVPN. Make sure to install and test them before arriving in China, as VPN websites are usually blocked there.
  • The Trip.com app is extremely useful, you can book everything from flights and trains to hotels and activities directly from it. It supports English, accepts international payment cards, and usually offers better prices than foreign apps.
  • Open a Chinese bank account. This is extremely important. Many popular Chinese platforms such as Taobao (the main online shopping website) don’t always accept foreign cards, and WeChat Pay or Alipay charge small fees when using international cards. Having a local bank account allows you to transfer money easily from your foreign account, convert euros to yuan, and avoid extra charges. It’s also much more convenient in daily life: without a Chinese card, you can’t send money to friends through WeChat, which makes it complicated to split bills or reimburse someone after a restaurant or a trip. Opening an account at ICBC, Bank of China, or China Construction Bank is usually straightforward, as long as you bring your passport and student card.
  • Take slow trains to travel around China; for long trips, take a sleeping train to make the journey feel quicker. China has excellent and affordable high-speed trains, making it easy to visit places like Shanghai, Xi’An, Hangzhou, Chengdu, or Harbin.
  • Download WeChat and Alipay, they’re essential for daily life in China (payments, communication, deliveries, etc.). You can link them to an international bank card like Wise or Revolut. Other useful apps include: Taobao (equivalent of Amazon), Tencen map or Gaode map, Meituan, Didi (taxis—don’t take the one at the airport!), Xiao Hong Shu (equivalent of Instagram), Ctrip.
